comment: The section requires a minimum actor and role set, but the examples remain institution-centred. A national role schema should distinguish the individual from people acting with or for the individual. Relationship alone must not confer access: a spouse, adult child, caregiver, legal guardian and assisted-access agent may each have different authority, scope and duration.

public.text: The section requires a minimum actor and role set, but the examples remain institution-centred. A national role schema should distinguish the individual from people acting with or for the individual. Relationship alone must not confer access: a spouse, adult child, caregiver, legal guardian and assisted-access agent may each have different authority, scope and duration.
public.suggestedRevision: Add to the minimum actor set: individual; supported user; authorised representative or proxy; informal caregiver; legal guardian; health or social care worker; and assisted-access intermediary. Require each authority to be represented separately from the relationship, with scope, purpose, duration, permitted actions, provenance and revocation. Standards-based patterns such as HL7 FHIR Consent and RelatedPerson should be used where applicable.
